title: De eximio usu methodi interpolationum in serierum doctrina

deep.reconstruction:
Euler continues the introduction of E555, the paper on the use of interpolation in the theory of series. To cut down the infinitely many curves through given points, he restricts the interpolating relation to odd power series, y = αx + βx^3 + γx^5 + ... . Such a curve is symmetric about the origin, so y(-x) = -y(x).

Problem I: given nodes x = a, b, c, d, ... with values y = p, q, r, s, ..., find the coefficients.

He rewrites the series in Newton form in the variable x^2:
y = x[A + B(x^2-a^2) + C(x^2-a^2)(x^2-b^2) + D(x^2-a^2)(x^2-b^2)(x^2-c^2) + ...].
The conditions then become a triangular system:
- p/a = A
- q/b = A + B(b^2-a^2)
- r/c = A + B(c^2-a^2) + C(c^2-a^2)(c^2-b^2)
- and so on.

He eliminates successively. Subtract the first equation from each later one and divide by the coefficient of B. This gives:
- q' = (aq-bp)/(ab(b^2-a^2)) = B
- r' = (ar-cp)/(ac(c^2-a^2)) = B + C(c^2-b^2)
- s' = B + C(d^2-b^2) + D(d^2-b^2)(d^2-c^2)
The next step gives r'' = (r'-q')/(c^2-b^2) = C and s'' = (s'-q')/(d^2-b^2) = C + D(d^2-c^2). The last gives D = (s''-r'')/(d^2-c^2).

He then systematises this. Set P = p/a, Q = q/b, R = r/c, S = s/d, .... The next page forms the tableau Q' = (Q-P)/(b^2-a^2), R'' = (R'-Q')/(c^2-b^2), .... Thus A, B, C, D, ... are the successive divided differences of the function y/x taken at the nodes a^2, b^2, c^2, ....

In modern terms this is Newton divided-difference interpolation of g(t) = y/x as a polynomial in t = x^2, used to build an odd interpolant. The construction serves the later problems of the paper, where Euler interpolates specific data to obtain power-series expansions.
errors: None found. The formulas q' = (aq-bp)/(ab(bb-aa)), r' = (ar-cp)/(ac(cc-aa)), r'' = (r'-q')/(cc-bb), s'' = (s'-q')/(dd-bb) and D = (s''-r'')/(dd-cc) are all consistent with Newton divided differences of y/x in the variable x^2. The scheme implicitly assumes nonzero nodes with distinct squares (a ≠ 0, a^2 ≠ b^2, ...), which Euler does not state.

ideas.what: Restriction of the interpolating function to odd power series, so the data at -x is the negative of the data at x
Newton form in x^2 for y/x, solved by a successive elimination tableau
ideas.modern_name: Newton divided differences (here of y/x in the variable x^2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Newton (Principia Book III Lemma 5; Methodus differentialis, 1711)
ideas.where_published: Euler uses Newtonian interpolation in several papers, e.g. E555 and his interpolation papers; exact list unsure

ideas.what: Successive-elimination triangular scheme computing the coefficients

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard application of Newton divided differences to odd functions via the substitution t = x^2. It is correct and routine; the interesting applications come in the later problems of E555, not on this page.
